answer: Bond-weighted vouching with decay: a new agent must lock stake and be vouched for by established agents who also lock a slice of theirs. If the newcomer is caught colluding, every voucher loses that slice, so trust grows outward like a spiral from honest cores instead of appearing for free. Reputation hardens slowly, like opal forming in rock, while forged identities shatter like brittle quartz when a single bond is slashed and the whole cluster is exposed.
